OPERATION EMPOWER — B2.11: PROJECT LAUNCHPAD
FULL PARTNER PROGRAMME COMPLETION, PRODUCTION REMEDIATION AND LAUNCH CERTIFICATION
1. Mission
You are acting as ScaleSmiths' principal software engineer, QA lead, security engineer, DevOps engineer and product experience specialist.
Your assignment is to take the entire ScaleSmiths Independent Partner Programme from its current partially operational production state to a complete, polished, secure, commercially functional and production-certified platform capable of onboarding and supporting real partners.
This is not a planning exercise.
You are authorised to inspect, implement, repair, test, commit, merge and deploy the necessary changes, subject to existing security controls, founder approval requirements and commercial safeguards.
Complete as much of this assignment as possible in one continuous execution. Do not unnecessarily divide the work into separate prompts or repeatedly request permission to continue.
Where a genuine founder decision or approval is required, isolate that dependency, document it precisely and continue with all other independent work.
2. Repository and production environment
Repository:
https://github.com/TheFridey/ScaleSmiths
Public website:
https://www.scalesmiths.co.uk
Partner portal:
https://partners.scalesmiths.co.uk
Founder administration:
https://admin.scalesmiths.co.uk
Canonical production repository:
`/var/www/scalesmiths/ScaleSmiths`
Previously verified production release:
`/var/www/scalesmiths/releases/3f2d6497d6fba7b00968043a68f1987b10467151`
B2.10 was merged through PR #179.
Verify the current production release, repository HEAD, environment configuration, running processes and infrastructure before making changes. Do not assume the previously recorded state remains current.
Review all relevant EMPOWER, AEGIS, ASCEND and EXPANSION documentation, including:

* FOUNDER-LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md
* PRODUCTION-FEATURE-MATRIX.md
* PARTNER-ACTIVATION-RUNBOOK.md
* AGREEMENT-PUBLICATION-WORKFLOW.md
* CONTENT-PUBLICATION-REGISTER.md
* B2-10-PARTNER-LAUNCH-REPORT.md

Preserve all existing functionality and security guarantees.
3. Known production findings
The following findings were established during the production audit on 25 November 2026. Reverify them before acting.

* Master Partner Agreement V4.1 is published.
* Published agreement fingerprint: `ff4977e34b153a8a1cd42c79491215103d23fe592b3a711aa84fa126da90e48a`.
* The founders have confirmed that the legal documents have been reviewed.
* The agreement has been issued to the existing test partner.
* Partner agreement scrolling was broken.
* A temporary production CSS hotfix corrected the scrolling issue.
* Cloudflare cached the previous immutable stylesheet and required a targeted purge.
* The user subsequently confirmed that scrolling works.
* The source correction has not been committed.
* A separate production build failed during ASCEND page-data collection.
* Partner applications are enabled.
* Partner email is enabled.
* Founder content management is enabled.
* Partner activation is disabled or absent from the environment.
* Enhanced pipeline and qualification are disabled.
* Partner performance is disabled.
* Delivery handoffs are disabled.
* Academy, Resource Centre, Knowledge Base, Objection Handling and unified guidance are disabled.
* Public partner profile publication is disabled.
* No approved market records were present.
* No withdrawal policy records were present.
* No agreement acceptances were recorded at the time of inspection.
* The production Content Studio contained only the published agreement.
* Prepared curriculum content had not been imported.
* Canonical and deployed environment configurations showed no governed-switch drift.
* One agreement reissue email was recorded as sent.
* One earlier application notification was recorded as disabled.
* The delivery handoffs page appears susceptible to the same scrolling fault as the agreement page.
* The public recruitment website contains planned-feature descriptions requiring reconciliation with current capabilities.

Treat these as investigation starting points, not unquestionable facts.
WORKSTREAM A — PRODUCTION ENGINEERING AND DEPLOYMENT REPAIR
A1. Establish a reliable production baseline
Inspect:

* Git status, branches, HEAD and deployed commit.
* Existing local modifications and untracked files.
* PM2 processes.
* Nginx routing.
* Cloudflare configuration.
* Canonical and release environment files.
* PostgreSQL connectivity and migrations.
* Application health endpoints.
* Disk space, memory and build capacity.
* Existing backups and rollback procedures.
* Failed build logs and abandoned hotfix directories.

Investigate any unexplained differences between the canonical repository and deployed release.
Do not discard legitimate uncommitted work.
A2. Permanently resolve the scrolling defect
Investigate the global `overflow: hidden` body rule and all partner-facing layouts.
Implement a permanent source-level solution covering:

* Partner agreement.
* Academy.
* Individual course pages.
* Resource Centre.
* Individual resources.
* Knowledge Base.
* Objection Handling.
* Guidance.
* Pipeline.
* Performance.
* Delivery handoffs.
* Activation.
* Password recovery.
* Applicant withdrawal.
* Partner workspace.
* Founder workspace where applicable.

Ensure that:

* Every page scrolls correctly.
* All content and actions remain reachable.
* Nested scrolling is avoided unless genuinely beneficial.
* Long documents remain readable.
* Mobile browser viewport changes are handled.
* Keyboard navigation works.
* Touch scrolling works.
* Modal and drawer scrolling works.
* Existing founder dashboard layouts are preserved.

Replace the temporary compiled CSS modification with a properly committed and built source correction.
A3. Repair the production build
Investigate the failed ASCEND page-data collection and identify the actual root cause.
Check:

* Shared repository dependencies.
* Build-time environment requirements.
* Database initialisation.
* Server-only imports.
* Static versus dynamic route configuration.
* Next.js build behaviour.
* Runtime dependency resolution.
* Differences between CI and production build environments.

Do not disable ASCEND functionality, remove security checks or suppress legitimate build failures merely to obtain a successful build.
Produce a clean, reproducible production build from a fresh release directory.
A4. Deployment reliability
Ensure:

* Immutable asset filenames change when content changes.
* Cloudflare does not serve stale assets after deployment.
* Previous assets remain available during safe transitions where necessary.
* Health checks occur before traffic cutover.
* Environment drift checks pass.
* Database migrations are safe.
* Backups are verified.
* Rollback is documented and executable.
* Production release identifiers accurately represent deployed code.

Clean up abandoned build processes and directories only after confirming they are not required by active services or rollback procedures.
WORKSTREAM B — PUBLIC RECRUITMENT WEBSITE
B1. Audit every public partner-related page
Inspect:

* Main website partner recruitment entry points.
* Header and footer navigation.
* Become a Partner page.
* Digital Growth Partnership page.
* Application form.
* Application confirmation.
* Commission calculator.
* Frequently asked questions.
* Benefits and rewards.
* Programme requirements.
* Privacy notices.
* Applicant withdrawal.
* Partner login links.
* Public partner profile routes.
* Relevant contact and legal pages.

Test every button, link, form, validation message and responsive layout.
B2. Reconcile public claims with actual functionality
Review every statement concerning:

* Commission.
* Payment timing.
* Withdrawals.
* Partner tools.
* Academy.
* Resources.
* Referral rewards.
* Achievement rewards.
* International eligibility.
* Partner email addresses.
* Business cards.
* Personal partner pages.
* Website demonstrations.
* Website Intelligence.
* Sales Studio.
* Founder support.
* Technical support.

Ensure each feature is described accurately as:

1. Available now.
2. Available after eligibility or approval.
3. Available through manual fulfilment.
4. In development.
5. Planned.

Never describe a feature as operational when it is not.
Do not silently alter commercial terms or contractual promises to make implementation easier.
B3. Recruitment experience
Ensure the public recruitment journey is professional, persuasive and transparent.
Verify:

* Application form validation.
* Duplicate application handling.
* Privacy consent recording.
* Accessibility.
* Mobile usability.
* Successful submission.
* Application acknowledgement.
* Founder notification.
* Clear next steps.
* Failure recovery.
* Applicant withdrawal.
* Rate limiting and abuse prevention.

Use controlled synthetic applications for testing. Do not send unsolicited messages to genuine applicants.
WORKSTREAM C — AGREEMENTS AND PARTNER ACTIVATION
C1. Verify Master Agreement V4.1
Confirm:

* Published status.
* Current review date.
* Correct fingerprint.
* Complete contractual wording.
* All clauses present.
* Correct company details.
* Version history.
* Legal review reference.
* Founder approval records.
* Partner-specific agreement assignment.
* Agreement acceptance history.
* Downloadable agreement availability.

Do not silently modify the published agreement.
Any contractual amendment must follow the existing versioning, review, approval and publication process.
The founders have confirmed that legal review has occurred. Do not reintroduce misleading statements suggesting that review is still outstanding. Do not fabricate legal approval evidence.
C2. Executed agreement completeness
Investigate the partner identity and effective-date placeholders visible in the agreement.
Determine whether the execution process records and associates:

* Full legal name.
* Entity type.
* Address.
* Email address.
* Signatory identity.
* Signatory authority.
* Effective date.
* Applicable jurisdiction.
* Applicable jurisdiction addendum.
* Agreement version.
* Agreement fingerprint.
* Acceptance timestamp.
* Company approval and execution records.

Ensure that the executed agreement record is complete, attributable, reproducible and downloadable.
Preserve the immutable published master text and its fingerprint. If partner-specific execution details are stored separately, ensure they are clearly associated with the accepted agreement.
Do not fabricate signatures, dates, approvals or identity information.
C3. Agreement experience
Verify:

* Complete document readability.
* Desktop and mobile scrolling.
* Acceptance checkbox.
* Signatory fields.
* Validation.
* Acceptance confirmation.
* Download functionality.
* Agreement history.
* Reissued agreement handling.
* Expired or superseded agreement handling.
* Duplicate acceptance protection.
* Stale browser session handling.

C4. Market configuration
Inspect the market approval system.
Prepare the United Kingdom market configuration using the existing supported workflow.
Verify all required reviews and approval gates.
Where genuine founder or legal approval is required, present the exact records and actions needed. Do not manufacture approvals or bypass separation-of-duties requirements.
International applications may continue to be received, but international selling and activation must remain subject to appropriate market and jurisdiction clearance.
Prepare a clear international expansion workflow, including South Africa, without asserting that any jurisdiction is approved when it is not.
C5. Activation
Once the published agreement, approved market and required founder approvals are verified:

* Enable partner activation through the documented runbook.
* Verify canonical and release environment consistency.
* Test invitation creation.
* Test invitation delivery.
* Test invitation expiry.
* Test invalid and reused tokens.
* Test agreement acceptance.
* Test password creation.
* Test account activation.
* Test initial login.
* Test onboarding progress.
* Test account isolation.

Use a clearly identified synthetic partner.
Never activate genuine applicants automatically.
WORKSTREAM D — CONTENT, ACADEMY AND PARTNER ENABLEMENT
D1. Import the complete prepared curriculum
Locate and inspect the official curriculum importer and all prepared content.
Expected inventory from B2.10 documentation:

* 13 Academy courses.
* 91 lessons.
* 65 knowledge checks.
* 13 resources.
* 46 Knowledge Base entries.
* 12 objection responses.

Reconcile actual inventory against the documentation.
Run the importer in dry-run mode first.
Verify:

* Idempotency.
* Correct content classification.
* Correct audience.
* Stable slugs.
* Lesson relationships.
* Course structure.
* Knowledge checks.
* Related resources.
* Source references.
* Review dates.
* Publication dependencies.
* Duplicate protection.

Import through the supported workflow.
Do not bypass content approval controls.
D2. Prepare content for publication
Prioritise:

* C01–C06.
* C08–C10.
* C13.
* R01.
* R03–R07.
* R09.
* R10.
* R13.
* Confirmed Knowledge Base entries.
* Approved objection responses.

Review R11 pricing against current commercial terms.
Reassess previously blocked content against the published V4.1 agreement and current operational policies.
C07, C11, C12, R12 and previously blocked Knowledge Base entries must remain unpublished until their actual dependencies are resolved.
Prepare the founder review queue so outstanding approvals can be completed efficiently in one session.
Do not falsely record founder approval or approve content using another person's identity.
D3. Academy experience
Complete and test:

* Academy homepage.
* Course catalogue.
* Course descriptions.
* Module navigation.
* Lesson navigation.
* Knowledge checks.
* Progress tracking.
* Resume learning.
* Completion records.
* Related resources.
* Search and filtering where supported.
* Empty states.
* Loading states.
* Error recovery.
* Mobile usability.
* Accessibility.

Academy participation must remain optional unless the contractual and approved onboarding requirements explicitly provide otherwise.
D4. Resource Centre
Complete and test:

* Resource catalogue.
* Categories.
* Search.
* Filtering.
* Resource detail pages.
* Download functionality.
* Version information.
* Audience restrictions.
* Publication status.
* Mobile presentation.
* Expired and archived content handling.

Locate the final approved partner handbook, jurisdiction addendum and other supporting documents.
Verify their contents and completeness before uploading.
Publish applicant-facing or partner-facing documents only to the appropriate audience.
The internal release checklist must remain internal.
A jurisdiction addendum template must not be represented as an executed or approved jurisdiction agreement.
D5. Knowledge Base and objection handling
Complete and test:

* Search relevance.
* Categories.
* Related answers.
* Synonyms.
* Empty search results.
* Approved answer presentation.
* Objection responses.
* Related resources.
* Clear distinction between internal guidance and client-facing material.

Ensure guidance is consistent with current pricing, commercial policies and approved programme terms.
D6. Unified guidance
Enable unified guidance only when its content dependencies are satisfied.
Test cross-content search covering:

* Academy.
* Resources.
* Knowledge Base.
* Objection Handling.
* Relevant operational guidance.

Ensure unpublished or restricted content cannot leak through search.
WORKSTREAM E — COMPLETE PARTNER WORKSPACE
Audit and improve every internal partner workspace screen, not merely standalone routes.
E1. Overview
Verify:

* Welcome experience.
* Partner status.
* Next recommended action.
* Commission metrics.
* Prospect metrics.
* Progress indicators.
* Notifications.
* Quick actions.
* Empty states.
* Accurate data.
* Navigation.

The dashboard should immediately tell a new partner what they need to do next.
E2. Getting started
Verify the complete onboarding journey.
Include:

* Agreement acceptance.
* Required acknowledgements.
* Account setup.
* Partner toolkit.
* Optional Academy learning.
* Support requests.
* Referral code availability.
* Clear completed and outstanding actions.

Ensure onboarding progress is server-derived and cannot be manipulated through client-side state.
E3. Prospects and pipeline
Enable the enhanced pipeline and qualification functionality once safe to do so.
Test:

* Prospect registration.
* Duplicate checks.
* Prospect ownership.
* Research allocation.
* Discovery.
* Contact recording.
* Follow-ups.
* Qualification.
* Scope submission.
* Information requests.
* Bespoke requirements.
* Founder review.
* Opportunity acceptance.
* Contract conversion.
* Rejection.
* Cancellation.
* Prospect protection.
* Partner data isolation.

Test all supported pipeline transitions and reject invalid transitions.
E4. Meetings and support
Verify:

* Joint sales meetings.
* Technical assistance.
* Training requests.
* Demonstration requests.
* Founder availability where supported.
* Request status.
* Founder response.
* Cancellation.
* Rescheduling.
* Notifications.
* History.

Ensure the partner always understands what happens after submitting a request.
E5. Commission
Verify:

* Commission statements.
* Pending commission.
* Verified commission.
* Held commission.
* Available commission.
* Withdrawn commission.
* Refund adjustments.
* Transaction history.
* Additional claims.
* Discount allowances.
* Currency presentation.
* Empty states.
* Error handling.

All figures must reconcile with the authoritative ledger.
E6. Achievements
Verify:

* Milestone progress.
* Eligibility.
* Qualifying client counts.
* Recognition.
* Reward status.
* Founder approval.
* Fulfilment.
* Duplicate prevention.

Reconcile displayed milestones with the published agreement and approved programme configuration.
Do not enable financial rewards without the required programme approvals.
E7. Referrals
Verify:

* Unique referral codes.
* Referral links.
* Attribution.
* Referred partner progress.
* Qualifying client conditions.
* Reward eligibility.
* Duplicate reward prevention.
* Self-referral restrictions.
* Abuse prevention.

E8. My partner page
Verify:

* Profile editing.
* Preview.
* Eligibility.
* Consent.
* Approval.
* Publication.
* Slug uniqueness.
* Withdrawal of consent.
* Unpublication.
* Public data minimisation.

Keep public publication disabled until the appropriate eligibility and approval requirements are satisfied.
E9. Coming soon
Review every feature displayed.
Remove obsolete planned labels when functionality is genuinely available.
Do not advertise unsupported capabilities as operational.
Provide meaningful explanations for eligibility-based or manually fulfilled features.
E10. Performance
Enable and verify:

* Performance reporting.
* Date ranges.
* Conversion metrics.
* Opportunity counts.
* Commission metrics.
* Achievement progress.
* Empty states.
* Partner isolation.

E11. Delivery handoffs
Move the page into a suitable shared partner layout.
Verify:

* Scrolling.
* Navigation.
* Responsive design.
* Accepted client projects.
* Published delivery status.
* Next steps.
* Appropriate confidentiality.
* No exposure of internal technical notes or other partners' clients.

WORKSTREAM F — COMMERCIAL CONFIGURATION AND FINANCIAL SAFETY
F1. Establish the authoritative commercial terms
Compare:

* Published V4.1 agreement.
* Public recruitment website.
* Commission calculator.
* Existing database configuration.
* Partner handbook.
* Training material.
* Financial implementation.
* Founder settings.

Known terms requiring reconciliation include:

* 30% commission on eligible initial build payments.
* 30% commission on the first qualifying retainer payment.
* £2,000 standard website build.
* £350 standard monthly retainer.
* £705 potential standard initial commission.
* £50 withdrawal minimum.
* 14-day commission hold.
* Two UK business days for withdrawal review.
* Five UK business days for payment initiation under the applicable contractual conditions.
* 90-day prospect protection.
* £250 qualifying partner referral reward.
* Contractual achievement milestone schedule.

Verify the exact wording and conditions in the published agreement.
Do not assume that this summary overrides the contract.
Where configuration is missing, prepare the correct settings using the supported workflow.
Where a commercial decision is genuinely outstanding, document it for founder approval.
F2. Withdrawal policies
Investigate the absence of production withdrawal policy records.
Implement or configure the supported withdrawal policy consistent with approved terms.
Verify:

* Minimum withdrawal.
* Hold periods.
* Eligibility.
* Available balance.
* Pending reservations.
* Duplicate request prevention.
* Concurrent request handling.
* Founder approval.
* Rejection.
* Cancellation.
* Payment initiation.
* Payment completion.
* Reconciliation.
* Failed payment recovery.
* Audit history.
* Invoice requirements.
* Applicable taxes.
* Currency and conversion fees.

Verify which payment methods are actually operational.
Do not promise Wise, bank transfers, international payment methods or automatic payouts unless the required operational arrangements exist.
No real money may be transferred during testing.
F3. Commission lifecycle
Test:

* Standard £2,000 build.
* £1,000 deposit.
* £1,000 final payment.
* First £350 retainer.
* Expected £300, £300 and £105 commission entries.
* Flexible payment schedules.
* Discounted builds.
* Free-build exceptions.
* Partial payments.
* Additional customer work.
* Refunds.
* Chargebacks.
* Cancellations.
* Duplicate payment events.
* Concurrent financial events.
* Withdrawal reservations.
* Reversals.
* Idempotency.
* Ledger reconciliation.

Use synthetic records in an isolated environment for financial mutation tests.
Preserve all existing database-level financial safeguards.
F4. Commercial rewards
Reconcile:

* Achievement milestones.
* Referral rewards.
* Qualifying clients.
* Reward approval.
* Reward payment.
* Recognition.
* Physical benefits.
* Programme versioning.

Ensure the platform cannot issue duplicate or unapproved rewards.
WORKSTREAM G — FOUNDER WORKSPACE COMPLETION
Perform a complete functional and visual audit of every founder section.
G1. Overview
Verify accurate commercial and operational reporting.
G2. Prospects and scope

G3. Resource library

G6. Recognition

G7. Web pages

G8. Programme

G10. Recruitment

G12. Content Studio

G13. Command centre

G14. Revenue intelligence

* Data sources.

G15. Delivery handoffs

G16. Automation
Audit:

* Automation review.
* Approval workflows.

Preserve existing ASCEND and MEGATON containment policies.
WORKSTREAM H — PARTNER TOOLKIT AND OUTSTANDING FEATURES
Inspect all existing implementation, planned functionality and manual fulfilment processes for:

* ScaleSmiths partner email addresses.
* Referral IDs.
* CircleCard.
* Digital business cards.
* Physical business cards.
* Branded polo shirts.
* Sales brochures.

* Fully operational.
* Implemented but disabled.
* Manual fulfilment.
* Partially implemented.
* Not implemented.
* Blocked by a third-party dependency.
* Blocked by founder approval.

Complete feasible first-party functionality and improve manual fulfilment tracking.
For external integrations, verify credentials, provider availability, costs and permissions before activation.
Do not fabricate demonstrations, testimonials, case studies or client results.
Do not incur new external costs without approval.
Provide an accurate implementation backlog for anything that genuinely cannot be completed during this assignment.
WORKSTREAM I — EMAILS AND NOTIFICATIONS
Audit every partner-related notification.
Verify:

* Application confirmation.
* Founder application notification.
* Invitation.
* Activation confirmation.
* Agreement reissue.
* Password reset.
* Applicant withdrawal.
* Meeting requests.
* Support responses.
* Relevant financial notifications.
* Relevant onboarding notifications.

Check:

* Resend configuration.
* Sender identity.
* Sending-domain verification.
* SPF.
* DKIM.
* DMARC.
* Link correctness.
* Email branding.
* Mobile rendering.
* Plain-text alternatives.
* Token expiry.
* Idempotency.
* Failure handling.
* Retry behaviour.
* Notification audit records.
* Privacy.

Use controlled founder-owned or designated test addresses.
Do not email real applicants as part of automated testing.
WORKSTREAM J — COMPLETE VISUAL, UX AND ACCESSIBILITY AUDIT
This workstream is mandatory and must receive substantial attention.
Do not rely solely on unit tests, HTTP status codes or source inspection.
Use an actual authenticated browser through Playwright or an equivalent browser automation system.
Audit every public partner page, every authenticated partner page, every internal partner workspace tab, every founder management section and every relevant dynamic route.
Test at minimum:

* 1920 × 1080 desktop.
* 1440 × 900 laptop.
* 1280 × 720 smaller laptop.
* 1024 × 768 tablet landscape.
* 768 × 1024 tablet portrait.
* 390 × 844 mobile.
* 360 × 800 smaller mobile.

J1. Interaction coverage
Test every relevant:

* Button.
* Link.
* Tab.
* Dropdown.
* Checkbox.
* Radio button.
* Search field.
* Filter.
* Sort control.
* Pagination control.
* Form.
* Modal.
* Drawer.
* Tooltip.
* Accordion.
* Confirmation dialog.
* Download.
* Upload.
* Navigation element.

Inspect:

* Default states.
* Hover states.
* Focus states.
* Active states.
* Disabled states.
* Loading states.
* Success states.
* Error states.
* Empty states.

Do not perform destructive actions against genuine production records.
J2. Visual quality
Identify and correct:

* Clipped content.
* Broken scrolling.
* Horizontal overflow.
* Overlapping elements.
* Unreachable controls.
* Inconsistent spacing.
* Poor typography.
* Weak visual hierarchy.
* Inconsistent buttons.
* Misaligned cards.
* Unreadable tables.
* Poor mobile navigation.
* Excessive whitespace.
* Layout shifts.
* Inconsistent colours.
* Confusing terminology.
* Misleading statuses.
* Unnecessary interaction steps.

Think from the perspective of a new partner who has never seen the platform.
The platform should feel like a premium, cohesive commercial product rather than a collection of development tools.
J3. Accessibility
Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
Verify:

* Text contrast.
* Keyboard navigation.
* Visible focus.
* Logical tab order.
* Semantic headings.
* Accessible form labels.
* Accessible error messages.
* Screen reader announcements.
* Modal focus management.
* Touch target sizes.
* Reduced-motion preferences.
* Zoom behaviour.
* Colour-independent status communication.

Use automated accessibility testing alongside manual inspection.
J4. Evidence
Capture screenshots of every major screen at desktop and mobile sizes.
Record before-and-after screenshots for material fixes.
Maintain a route and interaction coverage register showing:

* Page or screen.
* Viewport.
* Interaction tested.
* Expected result.
* Actual result.
* Defect discovered.
* Fix applied.
* Retest result.
* Evidence location.

A page is not certified merely because it returns HTTP 200.
WORKSTREAM K — SECURITY, PRIVACY AND DATA INTEGRITY
Perform a comprehensive security regression.
Verify:

* Authentication.
* Role-based access control.
* Partner isolation.
* Founder-only operations.
* Direct object reference protection.
* Cross-partner data access prevention.
* Session handling.
* Password reset security.
* Invitation token security.
* Agreement acceptance integrity.
* CSRF protection.
* Same-origin enforcement.
* Rate limiting.

# B2.11 deployment and rollback

Production runs PM2 release pairs, not the Docker release manager. Each release is a self-contained tree under `/var/www/scalesmiths/releases/<sha>`.

## Build a release (self-contained)

1. In the canonical checkout, run `git fetch` and confirm `<sha>` is the merged commit on `master`.
2. Create the release tree: `git archive <sha> | tar -x -C /var/www/scalesmiths/releases/<sha>`.
3. Replace `generated-sites` with a symlink to the canonical one. This is the **only** permitted symlink.
4. Copy `.env` from the live release.
5. Run `npm run check:release-env-drift` and confirm it reports `identical`.
6. Run `npm ci` **inside** `admin/` and `web/`. Never symlink or copy `node_modules`, and never copy `.next` from another release.
7. Run `node scripts/check-release-tree.mjs /var/www/scalesmiths/releases/<sha>`. It must exit 0. If it fails, delete the reported directories and repeat step 6.
8. Build each app with `node --env-file=../.env ./node_modules/next/dist/bin/next build`.

Step 7 exists because, on 25 Nov 2026, a tree with a symlinked `admin/node_modules` and a borrowed webpack cache failed "Collecting page data" for `/api/ascend/v1/operations/[id]/cancel`.

## Cut over

1. Take a fresh backup into `/var/backups/scalesmiths/pre-b211-<ts>-<sha>/`, with `SHA256SUMS`. Verify it with `sha256sum -c`.
2. Start the new pair on free ports (the next pair after 3400/3401), with `SS_RELEASE_ID=<sha>`.
3. Health-check on loopback: login 200, `/partner/agreement` 307 when signed out, and the web home page 200.
4. Back up the three `sites-available/scalesmiths*` files. Point `proxy_pass` at the new ports, then run `nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx`.
5. Purge Cloudflare only if a changed asset kept its old URL. Next's content-hashed `/_next/static` names change with content, so a normal deploy needs no purge. The 25 Nov purge was needed only because the compiled CSS was edited in place.

## Rollback

1. Point nginx back at the previous pair's ports (kept online), then run `nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx`.
2. To roll back env switches, restore the matching `env-before-*` snapshot and restart the admin process.
3. B2.11 adds no migrations.
